userStories.notes: Planning story completed. Generated 11 stories (US-48-002 through US-48-012) covering three user-reported bugs (socket timeout hang, iterative_match serialization mismatch, DNS circuit breaker) plus download infrastructure improvements (escalation integration in download_segments, retry queue network-aware classification, download progress reporting, segment deduplication, checkpoint restoration validation, config defaults for download_segments, download metrics collection, audio_first socket timeout parity). Analysis: download_segments.py bypasses core.py's subprocess+stall-detection by using yt-dlp Python API directly without socket_timeout; iterative_match.py:427 uses getattr(match, 'video_file', '') on MatchResult objects which lack that attribute; no circuit breaker in download_segments loop for systemic network failures.

userStories.title: Add network failure circuit breaker to download_segments stage
acceptanceCriteria: Add consecutive network failure tracking to _download_segments() loop with configurable threshold (default: 3)
Detect DNS resolution failures (Errno 11001, 'getaddrinfo failed', 'Name or service not known') and network unreachable errors as systemic failures
Abort the download loop early when consecutive network failures exceed threshold, logging clear message about systemic network issue
Reset the consecutive failure counter on any successful download
Add unit test verifying early abort after 3 consecutive DNS failures with remaining segments skipped
Add unit test verifying counter resets after a successful download between failures
userStories.notes: Completed. Added _is_network_failure() helper detecting DNS errors (getaddrinfo failed, Errno 11001, Name or service not known, nodename nor servname, Network is unreachable, Temporary failure in name resolution, No address associated with hostname) plus ffmpeg exit code 4294967158. Added consecutive_network_failures counter to _download_segments() loop with NETWORK_FAILURE_THRESHOLD=3 default. Counter resets on successful download or cached file hit. Non-network errors (403, removed) reset counter too since they're video-specific. Added 5 unit tests: DNS error detection, early abort after 3 consecutive failures, counter reset on success, non-network errors don't trigger abort, checkpoint before abort. All 27 tests pass.

userStories.title: Improve segment deduplication in download_segments to handle multi-segment videos
acceptanceCriteria: Fix deduplication key in _collect_matched_segments() to handle video IDs with underscores (e.g., 'abc_def') by using video_id directly instead of round(start_time)
Add overlap detection: if two segments from same video overlap or are adjacent (gap < 2*buffer), merge them into one download
Add unit test verifying segments with overlapping time ranges from same video are merged
Add unit test verifying segments from different videos with same timestamps are NOT merged
Add unit test verifying video IDs containing underscores are deduplicated correctly
userStories.notes: Tier: enhancement. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py:129-168 (_collect_matched_segments), src/stages/download_segments.py:157 (dedup key using round()). Current dedup uses key=(video_id, round(start_time), round(end_time)) which has two issues: (1) round() loses precision for segments that differ by <0.5s, (2) adjacent segments from the same video result in multiple downloads that could be merged into one larger segment download. Merging overlapping/adjacent segments would reduce the number of yt-dlp calls and improve reliability. Also, the _update_matches_with_local_paths at line 369 splits filename on '_' to extract video_id which breaks for IDs containing underscores.

userStories.title: Add checkpoint restore validation for download_segments stage
acceptanceCriteria: Validate restored segment files actually exist on disk and have non-zero size in restore() method
Filter out restored segments where the file has been deleted or is empty (0 bytes)
Log count of valid vs invalid restored segments for debugging
Cross-reference restored segments against state.matches to identify segments that still need downloading
Add unit test verifying restore() filters out non-existent files from restored segments list
Add unit test verifying restore() filters out zero-byte files
userStories.notes: Tier: enhancement. Files: src/stages/download_segments.py:392-416 (restore method). Current restore() at line 406 blindly creates DownloadedVideo for every *_*_*.mp4 file found in the output directory without checking if files are valid (non-zero size) or complete. A corrupted/partial download could result in a zero-byte .mp4 file that passes the glob but is unusable. Also, restored segments have source='restored' but no URL, making it impossible to re-download if the file is corrupt. The glob pattern '*_*_*.mp4' could also match non-segment files.

userStories.title: Add socket timeout and stall detection parity to audio_first pipeline yt-dlp calls
acceptanceCriteria: Audit all yt-dlp subprocess calls in audio_first.py and verify --socket-timeout is present (lines ~241, ~427, ~591)
Add --socket-timeout 10 to any subprocess calls missing it, matching core.py pattern
Verify --retries 10 and --fragment-retries 10 are present on all subprocess calls
Add stall detection timeout via _wait_for_process_with_progress if not already used
Add unit test verifying all yt-dlp subprocess command lists in audio_first.py contain --socket-timeout
Add unit test verifying subprocess calls include encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' per CLAUDE.md Rule 27
userStories.notes: Tier: hardening. Files: src/downloader/audio_first.py:241 (audio download subprocess), src/downloader/audio_first.py:427 (segment download subprocess), src/downloader/audio_first.py:591 (full video fallback subprocess), src/downloader/core.py:1571,1690 (reference pattern with --socket-timeout 10). The audio_first pipeline has 3 yt-dlp subprocess call sites that may or may not have socket timeout. Per prompt.md, there are 8 total call sites across the downloader. Core.py uses _wait_for_process_with_progress() for stall detection, but audio_first.py may use subprocess.communicate() with a fixed timeout instead, which kills slow-but-progressing downloads.
